neighbours.label: the verb ' fell', as opposed to dropped, rose or sank in the same sentences (a narrow part of this broad pole, not an account of it)
fire: In the parable, some grain fell on stony ground.
Hearing the verdict, they fell on their knees and wept.
Snow fell through the night across the valley.
Yesterday prices fell sharply on the news.
One by one the leaves fell from the old oak.
He tripped on the stair and fell against the wall.
Silence fell over the room when she arrived.
Then the old king fell in battle near the river.
quiet: In the parable, some grain sprouted on stony ground.
Hearing the verdict, they stayed on their knees and wept.
Snow drifted through the night across the valley.
Yesterday prices rose sharply on the news.
One by one the leaves dropped from the old oak.
He tripped on the stair and leaned against the wall.
Silence settled over the room when she arrived.
Then the old king died in battle near the river.
